ref_file_title: Den03 - A Designer's Guide to KEMs
venue: IMA International Conference on Cryptography and Coding 2003 (LNCS 2898), pp. 133-151
note: Generic KEM constructions from weakly secure (one-way) PKE, proved IND-CCA in the ROM; includes the re-encryption (FO-style) KEM that HHK17's U transforms generalise. cryptobib_key: IMA:Dent03; eprint 2002/174.

ref_file_title: EGL85 - A randomized protocol for signing contracts
authors: Shimon Even, Oded Goldreich, Abraham Lempel
note: CACM 28(6):637-647, June 1985. Preliminary version CRYPTO 1982, pp. 205-210 — cryptobib C:EveGolLem82, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4757-0602-4_19 (verified in vendor/cryptobib; cryptobib has no entry for the CACM version, so its DOI is from memory and should be confirmed by the reference-fixer). Introduces 1-out-of-2 OT and the trapdoor-permutation protocol.

authors: Eduarda S. V. Freire, Dennis Hofheinz, Eike Kiltz, Kenneth G. Paterson
note: cryptobib: PKC:FHKP13; full version eprint 2012/732. Abstract confirmed via WebSearch. Formalizes NIKE and its security models; cited as the reference for the primitive's stronger models, not as an improvement of the DDH reduction itself.

ref_file_title: FKMV12 - On the Non-malleability of the Fiat-Shamir Transform
authors: Sebastian Faust, Markulf Kohlweiss, Giorgia Azzurra Marson, Daniele Venturi
note: ROM proofs that the transform yields zero knowledge, and simulation soundness / weak simulation extractability, for Sigma protocols (the latter with quasi-unique responses). cryptobib_key: INDOCRYPT:FKMV12; doi:10.1007/978-3-642-34931-7_5.

ref_file_title: FLA11 - Benaloh's Dense Probabilistic Encryption Revisited
authors: Laurent Fousse, Pascal Lafourcade, Mohamed Alnuaimi
note: AFRICACRYPT 2011, LNCS 6737, pp. 348-362, DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-21969-6_22; cryptobib AFRICACRYPT:FouLafAln11 (verified). Also arXiv:1008.2991. Corrects the key-generation conditions of Ben94, whose original parameters can make decryption ambiguous.

ref_file_title: FLS90 - Multiple Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge Proofs Based on a Single Random String
authors: Uriel Feige, Dror Lapidot, Adi Shamir
note: cryptobib_key: FOCS:FeiLapSha90 (vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib, pp. 308-317). Journal version: 'Multiple Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge Proofs Under General Assumptions', SIAM J. Comput. 29(1):1-28, 1999, doi 10.1137/S0097539792230010 (not in cryptobib). Verifier: content confirmed via search snippets (NIZK for NP from certified trapdoor permutations for a polynomial-time prover, hidden-bits model, one string reused for polynomially many theorems); eprint/DBLP/ACM blocked by proxy.

ref_file_title: FO97 - Statistical Zero Knowledge Protocols to Prove Modular Polynomial Relations
note: cryptobib key C:FujOka97 (title, authors, pages 16-30, LNCS 1294, DOI verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib; Springer chapter page confirmed via search snippets). Introduces the integer commitment g^x h^r mod n and statistical ZK protocols over committed values; the computational assumption is a 'modified RSA problem', i.e. strong RSA (introduced independently here and in Baric-Pfitzmann, EUROCRYPT 1997).
